questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error from the given options.**

He was deprived from the benefits of college education owing to the death of his father.
questions.solution:
The correct solution is option 2 i.e. **He was deprived from**.

 [IMAGE: https://lh5.googleusercontent.com/2pwqSq5ph6_V_4RreQSjVc8VGchGTW2ZxWjFS545Q1cYsS5Fs8MsfDMaQe8bpbBLb2DctBPZiCUNndteRiIw9CElV07flM_r6n0VFH_Az_wv5ZuXUgdOCqz09Ywsrg3ORcVL_v4k] Explanation

__
 
• In the sentence, **'deprived from'** is grammatically incorrect.
 
• 'from' is used to indicate the point in space at which a journey, motion, or action starts.
 
• 'of' is used to express the relationship between a scale or measure and a value.
 
• **Deprived of **means to prevent something from possessing or enjoying
 
• Hence,** 'deprived of' **will replace** 'deprived from'** to make the sentence grammatically correct

**Correct sentence:__*** *He was **deprived of** the benefits of college education owing to the death of his father.

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

I would rather serve ________
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **than beg**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• 'rather' and 'beg' are **correlative conjunctions**.
 
• Correlative conjunctions are sort of like tag-team conjunctions. They come in **pairs**, and you have to use both of them in different places in a sentence to make them work. They get their name from the fact that they work together (co-) and relate one sentence element to another.
 
 
• For example: I would **rather** work** than** sleep.
 
 
 
• Similarly, in the question, 'rather' is present in the sentence. Hence, 'than' must fit the blank. Thus, options 1) and 3) are incorrect.
 
• Also, the use of the preposition 'to' is superfluous after 'than'. Hence, option (2) is incorrect.

Therefore, the correct answer is: *I would rather serve **than beg**.*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__***

 
• Some of the important Correlative Conjunctions are:
 
 
• Either….or
 
• Neither….nor
 
• Hardly….when
 
• Scarcely….when
 
• Both…and
 
• If…then
 
• Not only….but also
 
• **Rather….than**
 
• Whether…or
 
• No sooner…than
 
• Else…but
 
• Lest…should
 
• Other…than
 
• So…that

questions.question:
In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select “No improvement”.

Subhash Palekar a farmer received the Padma Shri award this year__ in his campaign for zero budget __natural farming.

options.text: at his campaign with zero budget
for his campaign for zero budget
for his campaign to zero budget

questions.solution:
The correct solution is option 2 i.e. **for his campaign for zero budget.**

 [IMAGE: https://lh5.googleusercontent.com/2pwqSq5ph6_V_4RreQSjVc8VGchGTW2ZxWjFS545Q1cYsS5Fs8MsfDMaQe8bpbBLb2DctBPZiCUNndteRiIw9CElV07flM_r6n0VFH_Az_wv5ZuXUgdOCqz09Ywsrg3ORcVL_v4k] Explanation

__
 
• 'in his campaign for zero budget' is wrong because preposition 'in' is used to express the situation of something that is or appears to be enclosed or surrounded by something else.
 
• **'at' **is used to express location or arrival in a particular place or position.
 
• **'for'** is used to indicate the person or thing that something is sent or given to.
 
• **'to' **is used to express motion in the direction of (a particular location).
 
• Here, in the sentence, the Padma Shri indicates his great work in his campaign. So, 'for' is the most appropriate word. 

**Correct sentence:**__ Subhash Palekar a farmer received the Padma Shri award this year__ for his campaign for zero budget __natural farming.

• Hence, **'the guests left' **will be replaced by** 'the guests had left' ** to make the sentence grammatically incorrect. 

 

***The correct sentence- **When he returned to the dining-room the guests had left and the servants were clearing the tables. *

__
 
• Let us know the meaning of the words given below:
 
 
• **Unusual** means not habitually or commonly occurring or done.__
 
• **Dynamic** means __characterized by constant change, activity, or progress.__
 
• **Useful** means __able to be used for a practical purpose or in several ways.__
 
• **Curious** means __eager to know or learn something.__
 
 
 
• " sacrifices have led to many (5)________ discoveries and inventions." . From this sentence, we get to know that efforts and sacrifices of science have led to discoveries and inventions that are used greatly. 
 
• As per the context, **'useful' **is the most appropriate word for the blank. 

**__Correct sentence: __***Science has made an (1) __enormous __contribution to the relief of human suffering, and humanity (2)__owes__ a deep (3)__sense__ of gratitude to scientists whose (4)__labour__ and sacrifices have led to many (5)__**useful**__ discoveries and inventions. *

questions.question:
In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select “No improvement”.

He spent all __which he has __in order to perfect his invention.
questions.solution: The correct solution is option 3 i.e. that he had.
